title: Discovering and Interpreting Biased Concepts in Online Communities
findings: In the /r/Atheism subreddit, concepts biased towards Islam were frequently categorized in normative terms like 'Warfare', 'Calm/Violent/Angry', and 'Crime', often revolving around specific people and news events. In contrast, concepts biased towards Christianity were more descriptive and generic, typically falling under the 'Religion' category and referring to doctrinal concepts like 'heaven' or 'sin'. The sentiment of language clusters biased towards Islam was found to be significantly more negative than those biased towards Christianity.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured biased concepts towards specific religions. In the context of the /r/Atheism subreddit, it automatically discovered and interpreted concepts that are biased towards Islam versus those biased towards Christianity, analyzing their frequency, strength, and sentiment.
